overall: Los Angeles is experiencing a classic marine-layer pattern overnight into early Thursday morning, with temperatures locked at 62.6°F since at least midnight with zero velocity — no warming trend whatsoever at this hour. Southwest onshore flow (9 mph), a relatively high dewpoint of 57.2°F, and persistent mostly cloudy skies are all signatures of a strong marine influence that will keep the day cooler than seasonal norms. Patchy fog is expected to linger until around 11 AM, further delaying any afternoon warming.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are in tight agreement: ECMWF at 68.2°F, HRRR at 68.9°F, and NBM at 67.0°F — all clustering in a narrow 67–69°F band, consistent with the NWS official forecast of a high near 69°F. The active heat and fire weather alerts (Yuma, El Centro, San Diego deserts, southeastern CA) are inland/desert events and do not materially affect coastal LA temperatures; if anything, the offshore heat gradient reinforces onshore marine flow, potentially capping LA's high.
max_temp_prediction: With NWP models converging at 67–69°F and the NWS backing a high near 69°F, the most likely outcome is a TMAX in the 68–69°F range, placing it squarely in the 68–69°F bucket. Cloud cover and fog burning off only partially (mostly cloudy forecast, not mostly sunny) will limit solar insolation during the key warming window, capping afternoon heating. Confidence is moderate-to-high given tight model agreement and a stable marine regime; the main downside risk is an even slower fog clearance keeping highs in the 66–67°F range, while upside beyond 70°F seems unlikely given the persistent cloud deck.
